"'''Shame of  the Sentinels'''" is a book located in Thalanaar, on a barrel beside [[Commander Anashya Starfall]].

== Contents ==
{{Book|Shame of the Sentinels|content=Centuries ago, the first Tauren tribes settled in the fertile lands of Multhan, harmonizing with the wild and untamed forces of nature, much like our own kind. These noble beings, though initially unrefined, held a deep reverence for nature akin to our own. The teachings of our druids bestowed upon them the knowledge of agriculture, animal husbandry, and even the written word. 
Their spiritual devotion extended beyond their own traditions, embracing Cenarius, and Elune. Thus, an alliance was formed, fostering mutual growth and prosperity. Though occasional misunderstandings marred the harmony, the Kaldorei and the Tauren dwelt together in peace.

----

However, the course of history took a fateful turn with the arrival of the Centaur clans from Morerume, now known as Desolace. These merciless forces launched a relentless assault upon the Tauren, seeking to dispossess them of their bountiful plains and banish them to desolate wastelands. 
The brave Tauren fought valiantly against overwhelming odds, but the tide of battle turned against them. Day after day, they were relentlessly pushed eastward, closer to the precipice of despair.

----

In a moment of solidarity, the Sentinel Army emerged to lend their aid in defense of their Tauren allies. United, they stood resolute, prepared to confront this formidable adversary. 

Alas, the true extent of the Centaur's ferocity caught the Sentinels off guard. Swift and merciless, the Centaur's style of warfare on open fields rendered the Sentinels' customary ambush and hit-and-run tactics ineffective. Countless brave sisters fell, their sacrifice forever mourned.

----

Amidst this dire situation, Shandris Feathermoon, burdened with a heavy heart, made the difficult decision to order a strategic retreat. The Sentinels regrouped within the familiar embrace of Ashenvale, leaving the Tauren to face their harrowing fate alone.

Ultimately, the Tauren lost their ancestral homeland, consigned to roam the desolate wastes of the East, forever marked by the curse of their displacement.

----

This grievous chapter in our shared history serves as a testament to our deepest shame, a betrayal of our noble allies driven by the fear of losing more lives. Indeed, we may have preserved our own existence, but at what cost to our honor and integrity?}}

== Auto attack == uses a loop to check if attack is set to auto-repeat. /run for i=1,120 do if IsCurrentAction(i) then return end end CastSpellByName("Attack") This one is decent enough but it is known to be unreliable if spammed. /run if (not PlayerFrame.inCombat) then AttackTarget() end This one is more reliable. but it requires auto attack to be found on the action bar. /run for z=1,172 do if IsAttackAction(z)then if not IsCurrentAction(z)then UseAction(z);end;end;end == Lightning Strike == If any shield (Water, Earth, Lightning) is active, then cast Lightning Strike, else cast Lightning Shield. /run local s={"WaterShield","SkinofEarth","LightningShield"}for i=1,27 do local t=UnitBuff("player",i)if t then for _,k in s do if strfind(t,k)then CastSpellByName("Lightning Strike")return end end end end CastSpellByName("Lightning Shield") == Earth Shock == Earth Shock rank 1, max rank if clearcasting /run local i,x=1,0 while UnitBuff("player",i) do if UnitBuff("player",i)=="Interface\\Icons\\Spell_Shadow_ManaBurn" then x=1 end i=i+1 end if x==1 then CastSpellByName("Earth Shock")else CastSpellByName("Earth Shock(Rank 1)")end == Far Sight == Spammable Far Sight /run if CastingBarFrame.channeling then if n~=1 then CancelPlayerBuff(GetPlayerBuff(0,"HELPFUL")) CancelPlayerBuff(GetPlayerBuff(1,"HELPFUL")) n=1 else CastSpellByName("Far Sight") n=0 ;end; {{RaceIcon|Goblin|Male}}{{RaceIcon|Goblin|Female}} [[Goblin]] | capital = [[Orgrimmar]] | language = [[Orcish (language)|Orcish]] | affiliation = [[Horde|New Horde]] | faffiliation = [[Orcish Horde]], [[Horde of Draenor]] | status = Active }} The '''Shattered Hand clan''' is an orcish clan named as such for the practice of self-mutilation that every grunt in the clan performs. ==History== The Shattered Hand had stayed in Draenor when the orcs first crossed the Dark Portal and were spared the defeat that ended the Second War. Under Kargath, the Shattered Hand and the [[Thunderlord clan]] lent their forces to [[Dentarg]] to reclaim the [[Skull of Gul'dan]] from a captain of the [[Bonechewer clan]].[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_Skull_of_Gul%27dan_(WC2_Orc) The Skull of Gul'dan (WC2 Orc)] Kargath later led a force of Shattered Hand orcs into Azeroth.[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Beyond_the_Dark_Portal_(WC2_Human) Beyond the Dark Portal (WC2 Human)] Kargath's Shattered Hand army defended the Azerothian side of the Dark Portal during the last days of the Invasion of Draenor, and they were left stranded with their chieftain after Ner'zhul abandoned them and the Portal was destroyed by the Alliance.[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_Dark_Portal_(WC2_Orc) The Dark Portal (WC2 Orc)] The Shattered Hand's status during the interim period between the destruction of the Dark Portal and the fall of the internment camps is unknown; of Kargath's contemporaries, [[Kilrogg Deadeye|Kilrogg]] of the [[Bleeding Hollow clan|Bleeding Hollow]] was captured along with his clan, while [[Grom Hellscream]] of the [[Warsong clan]] continued to evade the Alliance.''Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos'' Game Manual, ''[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_III:_Reign_of_Chaos_Game_Manual#Day_of_the_Dragon Orcish History]'', Day of the Dragon Supported by many of the veteran chieftains, [[Thrall]] ultimately succeeded in revitalizing the Horde and giving his people a new spiritual identity.''Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos'' Game Manual, ''[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_III:_Reign_of_Chaos_Game_Manual#Thrall's_Tale Orcish History]'', Thrall's Tale The Shattered Hand still exists, making their home in the [[Cleft of Shadow]], located in the orcish capital of [[Orgrimmar]]. The Shattered Hand makes a living as the Rogues Guild of Orgrimmar, now accepting various other races into their ranks, including jungle trolls and goblins. Based out of the [[Shadowswift Brotherhood]] in Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow, they are responsible for training aspiring rogues from various races in the ways of stealth, deception, and the brewing of deadly poisons.{{Horde}} [[File:Rogue (Class Icon).png|16px]] [16] [[To Orgrimmar!]]{{Horde}} [[File:Rogue (Class Icon).png|16px]] [16] [[Find the Shattered Hand]] Thrall acknowledged that the Hand was necessary to ensure orc and troll safety.[[Jes'rimon#Quotes]] "The great Shenthul" appeared to be considered a high-ranking member of the organization. The Forsaken Deathstalkers have allies within the Shattered Hand. The Shattered Hand was able to place spies throughout the upper citadel of [[Blackrock Mountain]]. Though the information gathering process was slow, they managed to discover that the influence of the [[black dragonflight]] had extended beyond the [[Burning Steppes]] and into the [[Stormwind (kingdom)|kingdom of Stormwind]] itself after [[Onyxia]] infiltrated the Stormwind court. ==Notes== * Both the Warcraft III Game Manual and the in-game [https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_New_Horde The New Horde] book mention that "many of the veteran chieftains" supported [[Thrall]]. The only chieftains who fit this description are [[Kilrogg Deadeye|Kilrogg]] of the [[Bleeding Hollow clan]] and [[Kargath Bladefist|Kargath]] of the Shattered Hand clan. The other clan chieftains such as [[Zuluhed the Whacked]] and [[Mogor]] were either in clans that opposed the Horde at the time or were on Draenor. ==References== {{reflist}} [[Category:Orc clans]] [[Category:Shattered Hand clan]]

== '''Shaman-related TWoW changelog''' ==

Shaman changes revolved around fleshing out the class’ melee damage and healing specializations, alongside tackling major issues within its ranged facet; through talent compression and overhaul, we sought to have their trees properly function as the framework on which the class’ diverse iterations could flourish. Rendering their capstones worthy of investment without stifling hybridization between the specializations.

=== '''Baseline Changes''' ===
Many of the changes you’ll read about further below aim to introduce quality of life changes to the class, both during levelling and in its gameplay at level 60. We aim to introduce these changes while preserving its mechanical and thematic flavor as well as rendering its progression in the endgame accessible to players without losing sight of Shaman’s ability to perform competitively with different pieces of gear and a talent choices spanning multiple trees. Mana cost reductions; increases to the duration of class enchantments, elemental shields and totems; allowing shaman’s enhancement-focused toolkit, namely their shocks and elemental shields, to also scale with a portion of their attack power.


Windfury Totem went through major changes which go as follows:

* The totem's effect is now an Aura, not an imbue. This proc only works for main-hand attacks, meaning that the totem works the way it did before this change but does not compete with temporary weapon enchants.

* The totem now only has one rank.

* The totem no longer grants an Attack Power increase on the extra attacks.

* This effect now has an internal cooldown of 1.5 seconds instead of 1 second.

* Shaman's imbues takes priority over the totem, meaning the totem does not affect the Shaman while any of their imbues is active.

----Flametongue Totem went through a few changes which go as follows:

* The effect is now an aura.

* Now stacks with Windfury Totem.

* No longer scales with Spell Power.

* Shaman's imbues takes priority over the totem, meaning the totem does not affect the Shaman while any of their imbues is active.

* The extra damage granted by this totem can no longer trigger on-hit effects.
''Developer Comment: We are more than aware of the value Windfury Totem brings to the table and how close it is to the hearts of players. However, its Vanilla implementation was too big of a percentage of Shaman’s overall output, pushing their personal performance down while it also made other temporary weapon enchants like sharpening stones or rogue poisons irrelevant. That’s why we decided to redesign these two totems to instead apply their effect in an area similar to other totems like Grace of Air, and lower their power since they will no longer be mutually exclusive with other temporary weapon enchants.''
----Totemic Slam (New Tauren Shaman Racial): Slam your target with your ancestral totem, causing damage equal to 10% of your attack power and concusses your target, reducing their attack and casting speed by 25% for 8 sec.
(1.5 Minute cooldown, 5% base mana cost.)
''Developer Comment: This new racial has been added as Spirit Link will now be the last capstone talent of the Restoration talent tree. This ability should retroactively replace your Spirit Link.''
----Weapon imbues such as Flametongue, Frostbrand and Rockbiter now last 1 hour instead of 5 minutes.
----Spirit Wolves summoned by Feral Spirit no longer scale with your Attack Power.
----New Ability: Earthshaker Slam: Slams your target with your shield, taunting it. Has no effect if the target is already attacking you.
(5 Yard Range, 10 Second Cooldown, 3% Base Mana cost, requires a Shield.)
----Earth Shock now has a x1.5 increased threat modifier instead of a x2 modifier.
----Earth Shield now has new ranks that can be acquired at lower levels. The current version is now the max rank. The spellcast pushback reduction is the same for all ranks, being 30%.

* Rank 1 (Level 40): 200 Mana Cost, 85 Healing on Ht

* Rank 2 (Level 48): 245 Mana Cost, 115 Healing on Hit

* Rank 3 (Level 56): 300 Mana Cost, 150 Healing on Hit

----Water Shield now has new ranks that can be acquired at lower levels. The current version is now the max rank.

* Rank 1 (Level 26): 34 Mana Restoration

* Rank 2 (Level 34): 55 Mana Restoration

* Rank 3 (Level 42): 76 Mana Restoration

* Rank 4 (Level 50): 102 Mana Restoration

* Rank 5 (Level 58): 130 Mana Restoration

----Chain Heal’s baseline cast time duration has been increased from 2.5 seconds to 3 seconds.
''Developer Comment: This change aims to steer Restoration Shamans deeper into their respective talent tree, as the new Improved Chain Heal talent reduces the cast time of Chain Heal by 1 second when fully talented.''
----Totemic Recall will now be available at level 10 and will correctly refund the mana cost of every totem. Additionally, the refunded amount is now displayed in the combat log.
----Windfury Weapon's cooldown between procs increased from 3 seconds to 6 seconds and it's proc chance has been reduced from 20% to 15%.

''Developer Comment: Although this might seem like a harsh nerf to Windfury Weapon's effect, it proved to be a major outlier during testing sessions, where Enhancement performed as an overwhelmingly strong outlier in its individual performance by pulling ahead of every single dps spec in the game by several hundreds of damage per second.''   

''Within the specialization's rotation it also completely outshined every other performance tool in Shaman's toolkit often making up for two thirds of the damage dealth by the spec, as if Enhancement now was solely the windfury specialization and every other spell existed alongside it.''  
''As a team we did not want to revert or diminish the scaling on shock and shields spells in order to keep Shaman in check, mostly because our aim with these changes is to bring the feel of progression to a specialization which has been desperately asking for it since its inception and it did not seem right to have these new and enjoyable tools pay for the imbue's overwhelming and polarizing performance.''

=== '''Elemental''' ===
We’re generally satisfied with where Elemental Shaman was after first class changes so it is only receiving minor improvements. Adjustments to this specialization aim to smooth out their random burst spikes both for player and creature combat, taking care of their threat issues, bump up their mana sustain and encourage the use of Flame Shock and Searing Totem into the rotation.
Elemental Devastation: Now increases your chance to hit with melee attacks and spells by 1/2/3% and your melee critical strikes increase your chance to hit with spells by additional 3/6/9% for 15 sec. Previous functionality removed.
''Developer Comment: This hybrid talent was moved up to 2nd row and repurposed to address both Elemental and Enhancement spell hit problems. Borne of Nature’s Guidance, this is a prime example of the aforementioned talent compression, while maintaining a focus on the talent’s utility for Enhancement, we felt that originally having to spend a substantial amount of talent points to earn spell and melee hit was detrimental to a class with so much variety across its playstyles, forcing it to thinly spread across the board; we are confident this change allows for more efficient and smoother gameplay performance for both elemental and enhancement.''
----Elemental Focus: Mana cost reduction Increased from 40% to 60%, 
''Developer Comment: Clearcasting is a big part of shaman’s resource management and we felt that as a talent it was incapable of properly addressing the class’ mana issues across the board, prompting us to increase its effectiveness. We see Clearcasting as a good example of the class indirectly increasing its mana pool as it acquires better gear, and wanted to push this concept further through this change.''
----Call of Flame: Now also increases your Fire damage by 5/10/15%.
----New Talent: Flame Guidance (5th Row Capstone): Increases the range of your Searing Totem and Flame Shock spells by 10 yards and casting your Flame Shock spell will now cause your Searing Totem to focus that target.
----Elemental Fury has been replaced by Electrify: Your Lightning Bolt and Chain Lightning spells charge you with electricity, increasing your Nature damage dealt by 2% and the critical strike damage bonus of your offensive spells by 20%. Lasts 20 sec. Stacks up to 5 times.
''Developer Comment: Replaces Elemental Fury with a stacking Nature damage and critical damage increase. While the upfront critical damage bonus is momentarily lost at the start of an encounter, revised Elemental Mastery will carve its place into any Elemental shaman’s rotation by quickly bringing them up to old Elemental Fury critical damage levels while making it worth it to do so through the stacking nature damage bonus.''
----Elemental Mastery: Now also gives you 2 stacks of Electrify buff.

=== '''Enhancement''' ===
This specialization suffered from over-reliance on their strong supporting capabilities, weak personal performance and a lack of enjoyable rotation resulting in Enhancement shamans were either taken solely for their strong Windfury Totem or that Restoration shamans were forced to specialize deep into Enhancement to provide their teammates with Bloodlust. That’s why both of these powerful support tools were changed to open up the possibility for Shamans to focus more on their personal performance instead of just being a support for others. The Enhancement tank builds also got some new tools to help them properly fulfil a tank role in levelling and early end-game content.
Rank 7 of Earth Shock and Rank 4 of Frost Shock now scale with your Attack Power, increasing damage by an amount equal to 10% your Attack Power. 
The base damage values have been reduced by 25 due to the base Attack Power values, meaning these ranks should do the same damage as before if you do not have anything increasing your Attack Power. The spell description of these ranks now indicate that the spell benefits from Attack Power.
----Rank 5 and 6 of Flame Shock now also scale with your Attack Power, increasing initial damage by an amount equal to 6% of your Attack Power and each tick of damage over time damage by an amount equal to 1.5% of your Attack Power, equaling to 6% with four ticks of damage. 
The base initial damage has been reduced by 16 and the base damage of each damage over time tick has been reduced by 4, meaning these ranks should do the same damage as before if you do not have anything increasing your Attack Power. The spell description of these ranks now indicate that the spell benefits from Attack Power.
----Fire Shock, Earth Shock and Frost Shock now enable your auto-attacks.
----Rockbiter Weapon now increases all threat you generate by 30% instead of generating a flat amount of extra threat every attack.
''Developer Comment: The two changes above allows both damage dealing Enhancement Shamans to include this spell in the rotation, while not diminishing their tanking potential when needed.''
----Ancestral Knowledge: Now increases all of your base stats by 2/4/6/8/10% instead of increasing your maximum mana.
''Developer Comment: The stats granted by this talent do not scale with any of your gear as they’re only your base stats.''
----Shield Specialization: The amount of damage blocked is increased from 5/10/15/20/25% to 6/12/18/24/30% to be in line with similar talents.
----Guardian Totems: Merged into Enhancing Totems.
----New Talent: Totemic Alignment (2nd Row / 2 Points): 30/60% of the threat generated by your totems is transferred to you.
''Developer Comment: This threat is further increased by all threat increasing factors such as the Rockbiter Weapon rework.'' 
----Improved Lightning Shield has been replaced by Stable Shields: Increases the number of charges of your shield spells by 2/4/6 but increases the cooldown between activations by 1 sec.

New Talent: Lightning Strike (3rd Row Capstone): Instantly strikes your target, causing 60% (Physical) weapon damage and 20% weapon damage as Nature damage. This strike also triggers an empowered version of your active shield, consuming 1 charge.
(10 second cooldown, 8% of base mana cost.)
Empowered means that shields expended by Lightning Strike benefit from your Attack Power, the amount of scaling go as follows:

* Lightning Shield: 4 Attack Power for 1 extra damage.

* Water Shield: 20 Attack Power for 1 extra Mana.

* Earth Shield: 15 Attack Power for 1 extra Health.
''Developer Comment: With these two talents we set out to tackle two of Enhancement’s issues, namely its inability to interact with its elemental shields in group content and the lack of another skill capable of taking advantage of the specialization’s melee-oriented stat growth. With both of these talents combined we are confident Shamans can now take full control of their elemental shields while being rewarded from their creative and effective utilization as both a damage tool and resource management tool; all the while having a second way of expressing their strength as a melee specialization.''
----New Talent: Calming Winds (3rd Row / 3 Points): Reduces threat generated by your physical attacks, weapon imbue effects and your Lightning Strike and Storm Strike abilities by 5/10/15%.
----Ancestral Guardian: Now requires 3 points instead of 5 points, now grants 15% increased armor value from items instead of 10% and chance to dodge increased from 5% to 6%.
----Spirit Armor: Now requires 2 points instead of 3 points.
----Enhancing Totems: Moved from the 3rd row to the 5th row and now does the following: “Increases the effect of your Strength of Earth and Grace of Air Totems by 8/15% and reduces the cooldown of your Grounding Totem by 1/2 sec. Your Stoneskin Totem's damage reduction is increased by 15/30% and additionally it increases block amount by 15/30%.”.
----Stormstrike: Now only has one rank, its cooldown is reduced from 12 to 8 seconds, mana cost is reduced from 12% to 7% base mana and now grants a buff that increases the damage of your next 2 sources of Nature damage you deal to be increased by 20% instead of applying a magic debuff that increases the damage of the next 2 sources of Nature damage the target takes by 20%. Additionally, you now need a weapon equipped to use this ability.
''Developer Comment: This change to the Nature damage functionality allows Enhancement to not lose their damage potential to other classes’ abilities and Nature damage dealt by weaker effects such as item effects.''
----Elemental Weapons now does the following: “Imbuing your weapon gives you a special benefit based on the imbue.

* Flametongue: Increases the damage done by your Fire Totems and spells by 5/10/15%.

* Rockbiter: Reduces your damage taken by 4/7/10%.

* Frostbrand: Increases the chance to proc the effect by 8/16/25% and becomes guaranteed to critically hit if the target is afflicted with Frost Shock.

* Windfury: If one of the bonus attacks of your Windfury Weapon doesn't land, your attack speed is increased by 10/20/30% for your next strike.
''Developer Comment: Through this talent we had the opportunity to work on the role of each of the Shaman’s imbues and make them focus on their niches more. Flametongue and Frostbrand Weapon imbues have been rendered capable of interacting with their corresponding shock, slotting respectively into a sustained or burst melee spellcaster capable of fighting from both afar and up-close.''   

''Rockbiter Weapon allows the Enhancement Shaman builds that specialize into taking blows for their allies to perform this task easier by granting them increased survivability for all kinds of situations.''  
''Windfury Weapon is left untouched as it falls in line with our concept of it acting as the imbue of choice for a pure melee damage dealing Shaman; while turning up the dial on this imbue would’ve been coherent with the changes applied to the others, we decided to instead have Windfury become more internally consistent by rendering it an inescapable menace for anyone on the receiving end of its effect, reducing the lows of missing a Windfury proc while avoiding rendering its power level polarizing when confronted with the other class enchantments.''
----Weapon Mastery: Now affects melee skills too.
''Developer Comment: This change allows this 6th row talent to feel much more worthwhile, buffing the damage of Stormstrike and Lightning Strike.''
----Bloodlust: Now only has one rank that grants 15% melee and casting speed, can only be cast on yourself, duration increased from 20 seconds to 30 seconds, and while under its effect, your melee critical hits increase melee, ranged, and spell casting speed of all party members within 30 yards by 5% for 5 sec.

''Developer Comment: Following the focus on personal contribution of the Shaman, Bloodlust was reworked to be a buff for the shaman first and foremost, while the party support component was reworked to depend directly on the shaman’s aforementioned personal contribution as well as its gearing progression; magnifying Shaman’s individual performance while toning down their reliance on buffing others to indirectly contribute to group performance.''

=== '''Restoration''' ===
We are satisfied with Restoration’s identity as an effective AOE healer and tank healer, with the power level of the spec being, to us, adequate; we’re of the opinion the tree in Class Changes 1 has nothing of value beyond nature’s swiftness and have found Mana Tide Totem was lacking the strength that is reserved to a tree’s capstone feature. Taking this opportunity for an update to restoration’s tree, we have decided to push for Chain Heal as restoration shaman’s identity and have tailored our changes around making the tree speak to it without leaving Healing Wave and Lesser Healing Wave behind; with this new tree we think we’ve struck the balance between the two souls of shaman’s healing kit, its slow-cast high value AOE healing and their slow-cast high output single target healing.
Tidal Focus: Now also reduces the mana cost of your totems by 5/10/15/20/25%.
----Totemic Focus: Merged into Tidal Focus.
----Ancestral Healing: Moved from the 3rd row to the 2nd row.
----Tidal Mastery: Moved from the 4th row to the 2nd row.
----Nature's Guidance: Merged into the revamped Elemental Devastation.
----Healing Focus: Now requires 2 points instead of 5 points.
----Nature's Grace: Now reduces threat generated by all Nature spells instead of just healing spells.
----Restorative Totems: No longer increases the effect of your Mana Spring Totem and instead reduces its mana cost by 10/20/30/40/50%.
''Developer Comment: This mana cost reduction stacks with the Tidal Focus talent’s mana cost reduction.''
----New Talent: Improved Water Shield (4th Row / 3 Points): Allows 2/4/6% of your Mana regeneration to continue while casting. This is increased by 1/2/3% for each of your Water Shield charges.
----New Talent: Undertow (5th Row / 2 Points): Your Healing Wave and Lesser Healing Wave spells have a 25/50% chance to restore a charge of your active Water Shield. When at maximum charges, this effect consumes a charge instead.
''Developer Comment: Our aim with Undertow and Improved Water Shield is to encourage the use of Healing Wave and Lesser Healing Wave by bringing its efficiency up to speed with that of other healers, a department in which the class is severely lacking. These talents are to function as the framework on which Shaman’s single target healing is rendered sustainable when used properly instead of restraint.''
----Healing Way: Moved from the 5th row to the 3rd row, now has a 11/22/33% chance of triggering from Chain Heal and now also increases the effect of subsequent Chain Heals.
----New Talent: Tidal Surge (5th Row / 2 Points): When you heal a target affected by your Healing Way effect gain a stack of Tidal Surge. Tidal Surge gives you a 15/30% chance for your next healing spell to refund 10% of the base mana cost. Stacks up to 3 times and stacks are consumed when the effect is triggered.

''Developer Comment: One of our marks was to have this new Restoration tree embody both sides of shaman’s healing; with Healing Way’s newfound ability to interact with Chain Heal we want our shamans to take full advantage of the options offered by their toolkit, while expressing their expertise through an apt and proper use of both it and the Healing Waves.''   
''Tidal Surge is the the other pole behind Restoration’s new mana-efficient ecosystem, we felt the class was too heavily punished for precasting due to the risk of causing high heavy amounts of overhealing, these two talents want to ease players into the idea of pre-casting and using their healing spells much more freely, by rewarding them for keeping a steady supply of healing throughout a fight.''
----Purification: Removed.
----New Talent: Improved Chain Heal (6th Row / 5 Points): Reduces the cast time of your Chain Heal spell by 0.2/0.4/0.6/.8/1 sec.
''Developer Comment: This last talent is the cherry on top of Restoration’s identity as an multi-target healing and its foundation moving forward. Know that this talent, specifically, is introduced in parallel with the removal of Stormcaller’s 5 piece set bonus, with the philosophy that items should add on top of a class’ strengths and not be the entire foundation of them.''
----Mana Tide Totem: Removed.
----New Talent: Spirit Link (7th Row Capstone): You link your target ally and their two closest allies within 15 yards together. When linked targets take damage, 30% is distributed among the other linked allies. Lasts 30 sec.
(6 minute cooldown. 15 yard range.)
''Developer Comment: This spell has been on our radar for a while and its popularity is felt through the community, when looking at its performance it had the power level akin to that of a capstone and given its popularity we opted to make it so. Having the addon makes everything more convenient, but is not mandatory. == FAQ == Q. What is EP? '''A.''' Effort Points (EP) are given for participating in raids. The EP number shows that player's activity. Higher EP = more active player. Seniority - how long a player has been in the EPGP system - also plays a part but is controlled by decay. Total EP can never go negative. Q. What is GP? '''A.''' Gear Points (GP) are given for receiving loot in raids. The GP number shows the amount of loot that player has received. Higher GP = player has gotten more loot. Total GP can never go below baseGP. Q. What is PR or EPGP? '''A.''' Priority Rating (PR) is the quotient or ratio found by dividing EP with GP PR = EP/GP. This is the number that defines the player's order in line of receiving loot versus other players. Higher PR wins over lower PR. Effort Points as the divident (numerator) and Gear Points as the divisor (denominator) means: Players that are more active (higher EP) and have gotten less loot (lower GP) have higher priority. BaseGP ensures that the divisor is never 0 and that new members or long inactive members don't get a very high priority upon joining. Q. What is Decay? '''A.''' Periodically the EPGP admin will apply decay to everyone's EP and GP values, reducing them by a set percentage. Since both values are reduced by the same fraction the PR remains the same but the next EP or GP added will have a larger effect. The reason for decay is so that old activity and gear received are not worth as much as new ones. In other words it promotes attendance but also allows a player that has gotten some high value items to catch up again over time. Q. What are the effects of a high / low Decay? '''A.''' A low Decay makes it harder for new members joining the team to catch up to veterans. A high Decay makes past efforts lose their value rapidly, and has the opposite effect: veterans do not have a big advantage to newcomers. The effect of Decay can be mitigated by staying active and is tuned to fit the guild's goal for minimum attendance. Q. Why is "Uber sword of L33t" so expensive (high GP)? Why is "Meh belt of Holy Resistance" so cheap (low GP)? '''A.''' The relative value of items is derived by several factors. # Item stat budget (a combination of the item's quality, level and slot) # Item desirability. How good it is for x or y class and spec. How does it compare to other items in that slot across tiers. # Item scarcity and source. What's the % drop. Does it drop from a difficult boss or trash?. # Guild policy. Does the guild want to encourage for example resistance gear acquisition? Lower price on resistance gear. Generally speaking a high GP value on highly desirable, low dropchance and high value items discourages "casual bidding". Only classes/specs that really need it will bid on it, everyone else will "think twice". A good price-list helps the system work automatically without officers having to step in often to veto bad decisions. Q. What is Off-spec GP? '''A.''' Items bid on during an off-spec / greed call by the master-looter will cost a percentage of their full price when won. This can be any fraction or even 0 (free). It depends on how much the guild wants to encourage off-spec gearing. Q. Is there an EP or GP Cap? '''A.''' The cap in EPGP is not a fixed number but depends on the maximum amount of EP or GP that can be earned in a decay cycle versus the % decay applied at the end of the cycle. For example if there is a weekly decay of 15% in place the new EP and GP value after decay is applied becomes oldEP * 0.85, oldGP * 0.85 then if a player can earn a maximum of 700 EP with 100% attendance the EP will cap out at X * 0.15 = 700 => X = 700/0.15 => X = 4667 EP. At 4667 points any EP earned in the week will be lost to decay at the end of it. Q. What is tier pricing?(raid tiers, not class sets) '''A.''' Guild can opt to adjust both EP awarded and GP of items in previous raids when progressing into a higher tier. This is to ensure that players are not discouraged from bidding on lower instance items for fear of losing out on higher tier priority and on the flip side that players will not try to "farm EP" in easier lower tier instances to use it for winning gear on harder higher tier instances. It keeps the relative value of efforts and rewards in check. Q. Are there items out of EPGP? '''A.''' This is a matter of guild policy. Raid craftable materials and patterns, Class Quest Items, or specific guild-wide effort items might be exempt from EPGP and decided by Loot Council or Class Leaders. (eg. drops related to Thunderfury, Sulfuras, Rhok'delar, Benediction, Head, Heart etc). == Contributors == * Roadblock (Author) * [https://github.com/wierdthing wierdthing] (Changes for Ret)

'''Shandris Feathermoon''' is a [[night elf]] quest giver located in [[Feathermoon Stronghold]] in [[Feralas]]. She is the General of the Sentinel Army.

==Biography==
===War of the Ancients===
As an adolescent, Shandris lived in the village of [[Ara-Hinam]]. When the invading forces of the Burning Legion arrived and destroyed the settlement, her family was killed and Shandris fled south with the other survivors, chased by the ravening demons. Fortunately for the refugees, the pursuing Legion was intercepted by [[Kur'talos Ravencrest]] and his combined night elf forces, who slaughtered the demonic army. The survivors of Ara-Hinam joined with the defenders. Shortly thereafter, at the defender's camp, a lonely and bitter Shandris was found by the priestess of the moon [[Tyrande Whisperwind]], who became fond of the young girl and couldn't bear to simply let her remain among the survivors alone.<ref>''[[The Demon Soul]]'', chapter 9</ref>

Shandris soon started to idolize her savior and followed her everywhere she went, learning the arts of divine magic and healing from the goddess-touched Tyrande. She wanted more than anything to take part in the battles, but Tyrande forbade it, so she secretly followed the Sisters of Elune into battle, looking on from the shadows. Her secret tours were eventually discovered by Tyrande, who told Shandris to never again put herself in such danger. Though Shandris reluctantly agreed,<ref>''[[The Demon Soul]]'', chapter 17</ref> before one of the most important battles in the war, she still grabbed her bow and ran after Tyrande after watching her ride away.<ref>''[[The Demon Soul]]'', chapter 18</ref>

After Neltharion revealed his betrayal and slaughtered both defenders and demons, until he was forced to retreat by Korialstrasz, the scattered mortal defenders were put under heavy pressure as the Legion renewed its charge. In the chaotic battles near the forest's edge, Malfurion Stormrage found his beloved Tyrande at the mercy of one he had thought dead, Xavius. When the first of the satyrs was about to strike the death blow to the young druid, his body was rocked by a feathered arrow plunging into his shoulder. Hidden in the forest, Shandris had proved her unnatural talent with the bow. When the satyrs attempted to open up a portal to Zin-Azshari, as the fighting between night elves and demons had reached their location, several were impaled by Shandris' arrows, allowing Malfurion to confront Xavius unhindered. Focusing on the wood of Shandris' arrow impaled into Xavius' shoulder, Malfurion caused it to grow into a massive oak tree, consuming Xavius's flesh in the process. Still, the night elf druid failed to rescue his beloved Tyrande from the escaping demons, and Shandris was rescued by Korialstrasz from the massive downpour created by Malfurion's resulting grief, and hounded him to rescue the priestess.<ref>''[[The Demon Soul]]'', chapter 23</ref>

With nothing stopping her from taking part in battles, Shandris clad in armor a bit too large for her, and joined with the Sisterhood of Elune. She followed the command of [[Jarod Shadowsong]], though the sisters themselves were now led by Jarod's arrogant sister, [[Maiev Shadowsong|Maiev]].<ref>''[[The Sundering]]'', chapter 3</ref> During the final battle, when the Kaldorei resistance met the vast army of the demon lord Archimonde, Shandris was in the middle of the fray. Along with the sisters, she dropped dozens of demons with lethally aimed arrows.<ref>''[[The Sundering]]'', chapter 20</ref>

During the Great Sundering in 10,000 BDP, Shandris fled with the other night elves to the slopes of Mount Hyjal. As the chaos subsided, Shandris stood next to Jarod, ever close to Tyrande.<ref>''[[The Sundering]]'', chapter 21</ref>

===The Long Vigil===
For millennia, Shandris remained at the right hand of Tyrande during the Long Vigil, and eventually came to lead an elite group of sentinels called the [[Shadowleaves]].

===Third War===
During the Third War, Shandris and her forces were stirred from their long vigil by [[Grommash Hellscream]] and the [[Warsong clan|Warsong]] orcs, who began to assault the forests of Ashenvale. During these battles, a vast army of fel orcs infused with the blood of Mannoroth managed to kill the demigod Cenarius after a long and arduous combat. Horrified, Shandris and the Shadowleaves retreated deeper into Ashenvale to warn the High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind, who quickly surmised that the invaders must leave. Upon sensing a looming darkness, Shandris believed it to be the demonic orcs who killed Cenarius, but Tyrande was still unsure.<ref>[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Enemies_at_the_Gate_(WC3_NightElf) Enemies at the Gate (WC3 NightElf)]</ref> While Tyrande took care of the human and orc problem, Shandris remained deeper in the foothills of Mount Hyjal, until her encampment came under heavy attack by the Scourge undead, which they barely repelled. When the high priestess arrived with the survivors of the demonic attack, she knew that the time had come to awaken the druids once more.<ref>[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Daughters_of_the_Moon_(WC3_NightElf) Daughters of the Moon (WC3 NightElf)]</ref>

During the Battle of Mount Hyjal, Shandris bravely fought back the demons and undead until she saw a massive demonic force amassing at the base of the mountain. Just then, Tyrande and Malfurion Stormrage arrived with human and orcish allies at their back, and united as the Great Alliance, they formed a plan to dupe Archimonde into destroying himself. Shandris remained at the side of Tyrande on the front lines, leading her forces to defend Jaina Proudmoore and Thrall's encampments. When the fortifications fell, Shandris and Tyrande, along with the rest of the night elves, retreated to defend the peak of the mountain. When Archimonde himself came, Malfurion quickly cast a spell that teleported all night elves and ancients to the safety of the shadowy forest, while thousands of wisps swarmed up from the forest and destroyed the demon lord.<ref>[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Twilight_of_the_Gods_(WC3_NightElf) Twilight of the Gods (WC3 NightElf)]</ref>

===World of Warcraft===
In the aftermath of the Third War, Shandris had been promoted to the rank of general of the Sentinels, and now resides in the [[Feathermoon Stronghold]] located on [[Sardor Isle]] in [[Feralas]], which is named after her. When Alliance adventurers met Shandris, she tasked them to investigate the [[Hatecrest]] naga's increased presence in the [[Ruins of Solarsal]],<ref>{{questlong|Alliance|43|The Ruins of Solarsal}}</ref> and later listened to their report of a strange gazebo in the heart of Solarsal.<ref>{{questlong|Alliance|43|Return to Feathermoon Stronghold}}</ref> While the heroes worked with her second, [[Latronicus Moonspear]], to deal with the Hatecrest threat, the general remained behind to assess their findings.<ref>{{questlong|Alliance|43|Against the Hatecrest}}</ref> Upon discovering evidence of a resurgent Silithid threat in the form of a Zukk'ash hive in Feralas, Shandris thanked the adventurers for their heroics on behalf of the stronghold,<ref>{{questlong|Alliance|46|A Hero's Welcome}}</ref> then tasked them to deliver their findings to an associate of the Protectorate, [[Gracina Spiritmight]].<ref>{{questlong|Alliance|46|Rise of the Silithid (Feralas)|Rise of the Silithid}}</ref>

===Mysteries of Azeroth===
Due to insubordination in the Sentinels' ranks, Shandris banished [[Commander Anashya Starfall]] and her squad to [[Thalanaar]].<ref>[[Commander Anashya Starfall#Quotes]]</ref> Following reports of strange events along the forgotten shores of [[Moonwhisper Coast]], Shandris sent an expedition under the command of [[Sentinel Commander Silverstreak]] to investigate.<ref>{{questlong|Alliance|54|Endless Vigil}}</ref> She was approached by Alliance adventurers on the behalf of [[Sentinel Briariel]], who was suspicious of the druids of [[Talonbranch Glade]] and discovered that they were researching how to obtain an extraordinary amount of [[Morrowgrain]] without raising any suspicion. However, as the Horde has been encroaching on kaldorei lands and with mutiny within the Sentinels, Shandris could not afford to be distracted by more internal disputes between the Sentinels and the Cenarion Circle, leaving the druids in Talonbranch free to conduct their research in peace.<ref>{{questlong|Alliance|54|A Sentinel's Rightful Suspicion}}</ref>

I wrote this out as my personal levelling plan after compiling a lot of different tips from discussions in the #shaman channel on the Turtle WoW Discord. Since I noticed a lot of people asking for one, I'll share this in case it helps anyone save time by not having to research the same stuff. I'll be editing this if I come across any more relevant info, and I'd be grateful for any corrections or additions that anyone is willing to make.

Big thanks to the following contributors who provided most of the knowledge compiled here: Squid, Zhafu, Rinzu, Peter Hammer, DemonBoyJr, Monolith, Akos, Not Normal, poto, Haaxor1689, Zaaparou and more (sorry if I forgot any).

== Race ==

All 3 races are pretty much equally well-performing here, so go with the one you find the most fun or aesthetically pleasing. That said,

- Troll is the best min-max race for PvE (quasi-Bloodlust haste racial for PvE, and hex is decent for PvP)

- Tauren is the best for PvP and the most tanky for leveling (+5% hp, nature resist) - Warstomp is the best PvP racial + Plainsrunning is the biggest QoL racial in the game (saves us 2 talents on imp Ghost Wolf as well)

- Orc is still a decent choice for Enhance PvE (axe skill helps + Blood Fury)

== Gear & Stat Prios ==

- Stats for tanking while leveling: +stam > +agi > +str > +int (when tanking at 60, +str becomes 2nd most important and +agi third)

- For healing: +int = +hp

- For DPS: +str = +agi > +stam > +int (+str & +agi roughly on par, at 60 +str is more valuable than +agi)

- Stat prios thread: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?t=21159

- For calculating AP: shamans get 0 AP per agi, 2 AP from str and 1% dodge and 1% crit per 20 agi

- A shield with high armor is a always a top prio, eg. Compendium of the Fallen quest reward -> SM Cath shield -> Gilneas shield / Mara goblin shield / SWV shield. When in doubt between two, choose the higher armor one (it scales with tanking talents that boost armor on shields by 30%, and all items by 15%). You can run an EHP calc just checking your % damage reduction on A shield vs B shield listed on your character sheet: EHP = HP/(1-%DR), then see which one gives you the most EHP. As a quick shortcut, in most cases, 10 armor is roughly equal to 1 stamina

== Talents & Rotation ==

With this build, you can fill any role in dungeons: tank, DPS or heal. We'll be picking tanking talents, but even if you solely want to DPS, this is arguably still the best build because you do practically the same DPS (the difference is really negligible) + have the benefit of being more tanky. That is, unless you're levelling in a group and don't have to care about mitigation. If you want to skip the tank talents, you could swap out Shield Spec. for Ancestral Knowledge. For healing, all you'll need is some +int gear and you're good to go for dungeons.

=== To level 33 ===

- 24p in enh: 5/5 Shield Spec > 2/2 Totemic Alignment > 3/3 Stable Shields > 3/3 Ancestral Guardian (before LS for mitigation) > Lightning Strike (take before AG if threat is a problem) > 1/5 Thundering Strikes > 2/2 Spirit Armor > 4/5 Thundering Strikes > 3/3 Elemental Weapons (first if feeling squishy) > Stormstrike (first if want more threat): (https://octowow.st/talents/shaman?points=-AoUYALAQDI-)

- Rotation: Rockbiter + Lightning Shield, using Lightning Strike -> Storm Strike -> Earth Shock -> Lightning Strike. You spend your mana at the beginning, then melee the mob down because you want to start the mana regen ASAP. Using totems isn't recommended, though Searing is probably fine if you're sticking in the same location long enough to get value

- Weapon: until Lightning Strike, a high dps dagger is just as good as a slow 2H; after Lightning Strike, a slow 2H is best

- From around level 25, focus on getting a good shield with high armor. At level 28, you can get the Compendium of the Fallen quest from Sage Truthseeker in Thunder Bluff (34.7, 47.8) and do SM: Library for the shield quest reward

- At level 33, get the Jewelcrafting +stam trinkets

=== Level 34-44 ===

- 11p in ele: 5/5 Convection > 2/5 Concussion (since few mobs do elemental dmg) OR 2/3 Elemental Warding (for mitigation in Maraudon) > 3/3 Elemental Devastation > Elemental Focus (Clearcasting!): (https://octowow.st/talents/shaman?points=FQAYI-AoUYALAQDI-) OR  (https://octowow.st/talents/shaman?points=FACYI-AoUYALAQDI-)

- Between level 35-41, try to get the Totem of Tides from the orc boss in Stormwrought - it's phenomenal for tanking dungeons + farming Lashers

- As a Tauren, at level 40, get Plainsrunning: head to the 2nd village you visit in Mulgore when you make a Tauren. The mount trainer there provides you a quest that leads to STV

=== Level 44-50 ===

- 6p in enh: 5/5 Thundering Strikes > 5/5 Element's Grace (raises threat w/o necessarily spending mana):  (https://octowow.st/talents/shaman?points=FQAYI-AoVYALAQDIAo-) OR (https://octowow.st/talents/shaman?points=FACYI-AoVYALAQDIAo-)

- Rotation: after getting Elemental Focus at level 44, Frostbrand + Water Shield, using Frost Shock -> Stormstrike -> Lightning Strike

- Optional: between 44-48, farm Earth Elementals in Badlands + occasional Uldaman runs to get the Goblin brainwashing machine for dual speccing (if the spot isn't camped too much, it might be possible to get the Goblin brainwashing machine for dual speccing, though this might be an unrealistic goal)

- Around level 50, it's pretty easy and worth it to get this axe: https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=51892 

- For the level 50 Spirit Totem quest, the trick here is that the Vultures have a higher chance of dropping the Spider Eye and the Black Claw than the spiders and the bears themselves

=== Level 51-60 ===

- Respec to 5/5 Ancestral Knowledge: (https://octowow.st/talents/shaman?points=FQAYI-FAVYALAQDIAo-) OR  (https://octowow.st/talents/shaman?points=FACYI-FAVYALAQDIAo-)

- 6p in enh: Bloodlust; 3p in ele: 3/3 Reverberation (take this before Flurry for more QoL in managing threat + more frequent spell interrupt); 5p in enh: 5/5 Flurry; 1p in ele: 3/5 Concussion: (https://octowow.st/talents/shaman?points=FYAYL-FAVYALFQDIAoB-) OR 3/3 Elemental Warding over 3/5 Concussion (Warding = a bit more tanky, but elemental damage is limited; Concussion = more threat):  (https://octowow.st/talents/shaman?points=FADYL-FAVYALFQDIAoB-) OR for cheaper totems: (https://octowow.st/talents/shaman?points=FACYL-FAVYALBQDIAoB-Ao)

- After that, finish every talent in resto except imp Reincartion, Healing Focus and Spirit Link: (https://octowow.st/talents/shaman?points=-FAAY-FoDoaIFYQKFAB)

== Lasher Farming ==

Here's a video on it by Zaaparou: https://www.youtube.com/embed/o90HvELvCpA Make sure to have a 2nd account with a level 1 -> invite it to the group, make it party lead; once you've finished a run, log out on your shaman, switch over to the 2nd account and reset the dungeon (click on the torch and it'll port you to DM: West entrance). Rotate Nova > Magma > Nova on each pack, heal up & drink between packs; during the pack, you'll have to swap to Earth Shield for 100% pushback protection + do 1-2 Healing Waves on yourself, then switch back to Water Shield. Basically, you do 1 pack at a time. Have Water Shield on, aggro the pack, drop Stoneskin, agility, Healing Stream. When the pack gets close, drop Fire Nova. Then use Magma. Usually, you'll dip to around 50% health at this time, so you can use Earth Shield + cast 1-2 Healing Waves. Switch back to Water Shield, Fire Nova when it's off cooldown, drop Magma again. Usually, the pack will be dead at this time, but sometimes a 3rd Fire Nova totem is needed. You should finish each lasher pack at like 60% health and 40% mana. Talent-wise, you'll need this specific spec with all the talents that increase totem damage (Elemental Weapons in enhance - Flametongue - for +30% damage increase to fire totems) and the ones that transfer totem threat to you (otherwise the Lashers will kill your totems), as well as 12 points in resto for pushback protection: (https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/c/1.18.0/shaman?points=FAAQ-AoUYALAQDI-FoAAC). Also make sure to have Totem of Tides from the new Stormwrought dungeon - it deals aoe frost damage every time you are hit while having water shield active. Gear-wise, bring +int/mp5 and +stam gear (e.g. the shield from ST - Eranikus; Princess Dagger - the blue one with +int/mp5; or just some green "of stamina" mace). A good potential farming trinket: Blood-etched Fetish (from RFD - Death Prophet Rakameg, 25% drop rate). After raids are out, stack some vampirism - around 10% (Drillborer Disk and the Rag Flame Trinket and totem). Having herbalism helps the gold you earn because you can potentially get Black Lotus from picking the Dream Foil in there.

== Tanking Rotation ==

- Goal: to save mana, never generate more threat than needed to maintain aggro - your primary job is to keep aggro, not deal damage. Try to match your healer's mana use rate to keep the pulls rolling as much as you can. It’s much safer to make sure you have the resources (mana) to save a pull that goes south than to spend everything trying to shorten the encounter. So whenever possible, skip using the rotation below and just do auto-attacks + taunt. Or downrank your shocks when you don't need to go all out. Especially avoid the AoE fire totems if possible. Rather than using Earth Shock on cooldown and being caught out with a mob running towards the healer, make sure you can react to any situation that might come up

- Imbue Rockbiter on a 1H and use a shield

- Mark your targets; the party should be focusing on your kill order to not split your threat thin. Put a skull and cross mark and only tag other mobs so the healer doesn't get aggro and keep threat on skull (if someone goes for cross before skull is dead, they can tank it)

- Always ask for Judgment of Wisdom on the skull if there's a pala in the party to help with mana 

- Totems: with >=2 DPS in the party, placing down a Windfury Totem is justified. Especially if they are higher level or well-geared. Just tell them if they rip threat, they tank that mob as a deal. With a pala, Blessing of Salvation (-30% threat generation) can also be placed on the melee DPS in exchange for Windfury. Use Mana Spring only if you're going to stand close to it for >20s

- You can use Lightning Shield for the pull for added threat, switch to Water Shield halfway through and switch back to Lightning Shield whenever Clearcasting procs. If you have Totem of Tides, you can start with Water Shield already during leveling, but Lightning Shield with Lightning Strike is still the best for ST threat

- Pull with rank 1 Lightning Bolt (big range, basically 0 mana) + Chain Lightning (to establish max initial threat). For real max threat, optionally add a Molten Blast after as it has a short cast time which you can fit in the time the mobs run to you

- Running in, you'll want to Stormstrike on target 1, tab switch to Earth Shock target 2, and Lightning Strike target 3. If a target resists nature damage, use Frost Shock instead of Earth Shock

- Tab switch between targets giving each of them an Earth Shock and melee auto attack. When in doubt, place a Stoneclaw Totem (though the threat per mana is great and allows you to passively regen and chain pull). Drop an Earthbind after Stoneclaw expires, if needed

- Use rank 1 Earth Shock to interrupt spells

- AoE threat for >3 mobs: Stoneclaw Totem, or fire totems - Fire Nova and Magma. If targets resist fire damage, Stoneclaw is your only AoE threat

- Oh shit: if a pull was bigger than anticipated or to quickly get aggro off healers: Fire Nova - huge snap threat, but mana intensive

- Mini oh shit: save your taunt to force a mob to attack you when it's attacking your healers

- When a mob gets loose or runs towards a sheeped target, use max rank Lightning Bolt for high threat or Earth Shock for big snap threat

- Healing yourself is a last resort; it's almost always better to pop Earth Shield, a Healing Potion or a Healthstone if you have one. If things get dicey, make sure to use those; never start casting while taking hits

- After a pack is almost dead, move to a new one and Earth Shock one of those mobs to bring in that next pack

- To kite melee mobs & nuke them with casters before they arrive, use Chain Lightning to pull and Earthbind Totem to snare them. Optionally Frost Shock to help kite. Earthbind also works as an "oh shit" button to help a healer catch up

- For Caverns of Time: Black Morass, bring a Druid, Warlock or Hunter to help CC the mobs during those 3/4 Dragon pack pulls leading to the first boss (this dungeon eats every tank; it's not a shaman-specific thing to struggle here). Having a pala friend is huge for devotion aura. When the last boss enrages, find a way to kite it. Aim for approx 6k armor and 4k hp unbuffed before tanking it. It's also recommended to get 4* the best armor kits and initially a fortitude and armor potion + health potion. Some cool items which can help you reach the needed mitigation: Hateforge trinket, even the lvl 33 stamina JC trinket, Hateforge tank neck, shield with the biggest armor you find (preferably 1900+), Helm of Narv (if you wanna buy a BoE), Kara Crypt tank ring, Naglering

-> With the new "Spell AoE tank" build https://octowow.st/talents/shaman?points=FQDYLAADAC-FAVYALBQDIAY-, if you really want to cook some threat on a ST, you can rotate in Fire Nova -> Magma totems and Stoneclaw, like you're doing AoE threat. But it's very expensive to do that so you won't usually maintain that (or need to)

== Enh DPS Rotation ==

- In dungeons while leveling, use a 2H with Flametongue or WF (*anything but* Rockbiter - at 60 WF) as imbue + Lightning Shield, using Lightning Strike -> Storm Strike, maybe Earth/Flame Shock on bosses -> Lightning Strike

- After Ele Focus/Weapons, use a 2H with Frostbrand + Water Shield, using Frost Shock -> Stormstrike -> Lightning Strike/Shield

- Totems: Strength of Earth, Flametongue, Windfury (once you have it) and Mana Spring. 

- Imbues: Frostbrand for some dungeons or soloing. Windfury is preferred for raiding and what you use when you’ve got a real weapon that you wanna do real numbers with.

- At 60 as you get more crit / focus procs, but be ready to chug mana pots and tea on CD to max damage to sustain Lightning shield longer otherwise you swap to Water shield when you're low on mana. Your mana consumption will also go down in raids, especially if you have ferals around. Blessing of Kings, Mark of the Wild, elixirs like Mongoose and Dreamshard, etc.

- Rotation at 60: use Windfury imbue + Lightning Shield; swap to Water Shield when low on mana. Keep up Lightning Shield. Don’t use Flame Shock on targets that won’t live more than 9-15 seconds. The point at which a Flame Shock becomes more worth than Earth Shock depends on your gear and level, so test on a dummy. At max level it’s always at least 3 ticks (9 seconds). For the rotation, put down totems first -> cast Flame Shock (or Earth Shock if immune) early when running in -> Stormstrike -> Lightning Strike -> Earth Shock (or Flame Shock to reapply debuff), repeat. TL;DR: FS/ES -> SS -> LS, repeat.

== Healing Rotation ==

- No imbue

- Put down totems that are most beneficial for your group, but only if needed to conserve mana (they have a 30y radius now, so sometimes you won't need to put them down again for a new pack): Strength of Earth, Flametongue, Windfury (once you have it) and Mana Spring (except when you need frost resistance and/or tremor/grounding). Situationally, use poison/disease cleansing, Fire Resistance or even Healing Stream totems

- To keep your tank up in dungeons, use the latest rank of Healing Wave and Lesser Healing Wave, and -2 downranked Healing Wave, eg. r5 HW and LHW + r3 HW. It's also recommended to use r1 Healing Wave sometimes just to trigger Healing Way procs and fish for +armor on tanks

- Chain Heal occasionally if there's lots of cleave dmg on the party

- Once you're raiding, all you really need is Chain Heal rank 1 besides dropping totems within range of your group. Besides that, you can throw out Spirit Link on tanks during enrage phases, eg. use on Maexxna before web wrap

== Totem Use While Solo ==

- They're not often worth dropping since you’ll be killing faster than the mana is worth to drop them (the mana cast is balanced around your whole party benefiting)

- That said, Earthbind weaving with a Swing timer is worth doing if you care about reducing the damage you take fighting mobs 1v1

- After getting Clearcasting, you can use Searing Totem + Stoneskin occasionally, mainly when it‘s possible to chain pull multiple mobs to the same spot

- To maximize your fire totems' damage when you have Elemental Weapons, you could use the Flametongue imbue - but generally Frostbrand is still superior while leveling

== Earthbind Weaving/Kiting ==

- Earthbind Totem > Searing Totem > Flame Shock

- Melee, side strafe through them (don't expose your back) to get out of their range while your auto attack is resetting

- As your swing timer is resetting, position to re-enter the mobs' hitbox and swing again

- Re-apply Flame Shock / Lightning shield if efficient

== Profs ==

- Skinning & LW while leveling since nodes are highly contested on Ambershire atm. And LW allows you to make Stormshroud armor around level 50 (especially the shoulders and hands, they're pre-BiS for enhance), and Devilsaur hands/legs around level 53/55 respectively 

- Alternatively, could take Mining & Blacksmithing as enhance; the Hateforge set is pretty nice around level 50; then after Kara10 comes out, you can get the Towerforge set -> you can also just buy these sets or pieces (chest and legs especially) from AH

- To be more economical, you could skip LW/BS and go straight for herbalism & alchemy from the start

- At ~53 when you start farming lashers, after making Stormshroud, drop LW for herbalism to beef up your gold farming by getting Dream Foil with a chance at Black Lotus

- At 60, herbalism & alchemy for general use and late-game gold (Black Lotus hunting is fun)

- Consider dropping alchemy for engineering - dropping Sappers/Dynamite will help your raid clear faster + if you plan to PvP there’s a lot of utility, even outside of stun grenades

== Spells to Buy ==

- You can skip all but 1st rank of Resurrection

- Can technically skip Flametongue imbue

- Totems: you likely won't use the nature/frost/fire resistance totems during leveling enough to justify getting those. If you want, you can probably skip all totems besides the Poison/Disease cleansing totems, though for tanking you might want the strength/agi/WF totems. Water totems are optional (pretty weak while leveling but can be nice)

- If you don't plan to tank or play ele, skip the ranged damage spells (but never shocks)

- Everything else you need no matter the spec

Eventually, the rule of thumb is to get 30-35% crit, then start stacking AP and +haste (the more haste you get the better)

- Tanking: focus on +stam and armor gear, ignoring defense beyond 15 (with the caveat that you'll still want defense, agility or direct dodge stats when it doesn't compromise stamina or armor to grab it). Generally speaking, just try to get the best threat/defense piece you can for each armor slot because sometimes you need to max your defense out, but sometimes you need a lot of threat, so it’s just dependent on the fight. Shields: SWV shield or the one from Kara5 are acceptable as pre-BiS. The one from BM can probably also be used (less stamina though)

- Resto: Get as much +healing and +int as you can. Just do all the high level dungeons a few times and you should be good, eg. get the legs from DM West, decent options from BRD are the gloves from either Emperor or Moira/Mantle of Lost Hope/Soot Encrusted Footwear/Guiding Stave of Wisdom/Second Wind, Rivendare's Robe from Stratholme UD, Royal Seal of Eldre'Thalas from Dire Maul. As for crafted items, the crafted cloak, and maybe even the crafted chest are great options if you can afford it. Black Morass has the BiS totem until Naxx, and some caster stuff, as well as Kara Crypts. I wouldn't recommend it since it's easy to get similarly strong items in MC/BWL/AQ40, but you could look out for high healing power lvl 54+ green gear on the AH such as Created Cape (you won't need to replace it until the cape from AQ40's final boss), the chest piece and maybe Corehound Belt (optional because costly) - some of those pieces are better than even MC T1 (for example the legs), but it comes at the cost of stam & int (on a badly geared resto shammy, int is pretty important; around a 4k mana pool is recommended - or if your guild clears raids fast enough, you can just drink more pots/tea and oranges between pulls). Enchants to get for resto besides the typically recommended ones outside of T-WoW are enchanted armor kits that give +9 spell power. 2% haste to shoulder enchant, and then 1% haste vs +12 spellpower to helm/legs; ring/neck enchants (+12 healing) from JC. Belt buckle for +10 intellect. Other ideas: the helm and trinket from AD faction, Mindfang from AB exalted, offhand from AV exalted, the shield from BM exalted, totem from BM drop, decent ring from BM faction if Urok LBRS ring evades you, UBRS trinket with AD trinket will be BiS. Strat chest vs BM faction chest could go either way. For weapon, the weaker +healing enchant. Tbh for pre-BiS, it's probably not worth it to enchant gear you're going to replace soon - especially the nitpicky ones like +100hp on chest and such (instead, you can spend the gold on more mana pots and teas). +12 on neck and rings when you have decent ones are worth since it's pretty cheap, then gloves/wrist/weapon if you have good ones

- Ele: check the pinned in #shaman for a doc with ele pre-BiS. Basically need 15% hit on spells, as much int and crit as possible and spd, hit > crit > spd > int. If you have some gold there are two pairs of crafted cloth gloves that are really good, one with crit and one with haste. T1 belt/wrist from AH. The blue crafted Bloodvine set but don’t spend to much gold on stuff you can replace from Kara10. 2% crit quest reward trinket and DM trinket. It won’t be hard to get Onyxia group fairly fast, then you can get the Horde head and a good ring. UBRS has two trinkets and a great cloth head. Gloves of Unwinding Mystery

- You could look at a Classic BiS list and use Atlasloot to check the new dungeons like Kara Crypts (eg. Crown of Shattering, and pre-BiS mace: Boneshatter Maul), Black Morass (eg. a very good mp5 totem), Hateforge Quarry (the Corrosive Core trinket is good if you lack +hit) and Stormwind Vaults (eg.
